headline: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: 12GB GPU Breakthrough
summary: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reportedly runs on a single 12GB GPU, challenging assumptions about model size vs. hardware requirements. This carousel breaks down the architectural efficiency enabling local deployment of frontier-class models.

slides.title: Frontier Model on a 12GB GPU?
slides.subtitle: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash claims consumer-hardware compatibility.
slides.body: A new DeepSeek variant reportedly runs fully on 12GB VRAM. We dissect if it's quantization magic or architectural leap.
slides.deep_dive: The AI community assumes frontier models need 24GB+ VRAM. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash challenges this, suggesting either extreme quantization (4-bit/3-bit) or a redesigned architecture with sparse activation. The title "Full or Fake?" hints at skepticism: does it retain full capability, or is it a distilled shadow? This slide sets the investigation.
slides.key_fact: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash targets 12GB GPU deployment.
slides.why_it_matters: Democratizes local LLM inference for engineers without enterprise hardware.

slides.title: Architecture Shrinks, Context Stays
slides.subtitle: Same context window, fraction of memory footprint.
slides.body: Previous versions needed 24GB+. V4.1 Flash fits 12GB via structural sparsity and weight compression.
slides.deep_dive: The core upgrade isn't just quantization—it's architectural. Think Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) with finer-grained routing, or Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) reducing KV cache. The model likely uses dynamic expert activation: only 20-30% of params fire per token. Combined with 4-bit quantization, a 100B+ param model fits 12GB. Context length reportedly unchanged, meaning KV cache optimization is key.
slides.why_it_matters: Shifts cost curve: run 100B-class models on RTX 3060/4060 class cards.

slides.title: Sparse Experts + Quantized Weights
slides.subtitle: Only active params load; rest stay compressed on disk.
slides.body: Router picks 2 of 8 experts per layer. Weights stay 4-bit until compute.
slides.deep_dive: Imagine a library where you only fetch the 2 books you need per question. The router (a tiny neural net) predicts which expert handles the token. Experts are stored quantized (4-bit) in VRAM. On activation, they dequantize on-the-fly to 16-bit for math. KV cache uses paged attention: blocks swapped between VRAM and system RAM. This avoids the O(n²) memory explosion.
slides.why_it_matters: VRAM scales with active params, not total params.

slides.title: Speed vs. Quality Trade-off
slides.subtitle: Source cites latency & perplexity; exact suites unspecified.
slides.body: Expect 2-3x slower than 16-bit dense, but 5x faster than CPU offload.
slides.deep_dive: The source doesn't name MMLU or HumanEval. Conceptually: 4-bit quantization adds ~1-2% perplexity. Sparse routing adds token-dependent latency variance. On 12GB GPU, you avoid PCIe bottleneck of CPU offload. Latency per token: ~50-100ms (vs 20ms for 16-bit on 24GB). Throughput drops but batch=1 latency stays interactive. Memory: ~10.5GB peak (model + KV cache + overhead).
slides.key_fact: No standardized benchmarks disclosed in source.
slides.why_it_matters: Engineers must run custom evals; don't trust marketing claims.

slides.title: From Cloud-Only to Desk-Side
slides.subtitle: Hardware barrier drops from $2k+ to $300 GPU.
slides.body: Previously: quantize to 4-bit, still OOM on 12GB. Now: architectural sparsity fits.
slides.deep_dive: Old path: take 100B dense model → 4-bit → 50GB weights + KV cache → OOM on 12GB. Must offload to CPU → 5-10 tokens/sec. New path: MoE 100B (active 20B) → 4-bit → 10GB weights + optimized KV → fits 12GB. Runs 20-30 tokens/sec fully on GPU. The shift is structural: sparsity is designed in, not hacked on via post-training quantization.
slides.key_fact: Designed-in sparsity beats post-hoc quantization for memory.
slides.why_it_matters: Enables local RAG, coding agents, private data processing on consumer PCs.

slides.title: Local-First AI Agents Become Viable
slides.subtitle: Run coding copilot, RAG, or chat fully offline on laptop.
slides.body: Teams deploy V4.1 Flash on dev laptops for privacy-sensitive code gen.
slides.deep_dive: Scenario: FinTech team cannot send code to cloud. They containerize V4.1 Flash with llama.cpp or vLLM on RTX 4060 laptops. Latency ~80ms/token feels instant for autocomplete. RAG index stays local. Cost: $0/api call. Ops: model updates via git pull. Risk: quality drift vs cloud model. Mitigation: nightly eval suite on golden prompt set. This shifts AI from SaaS dependency to software artifact.
slides.why_it_matters: Changes build-vs-buy calculus for internal AI tools.

slides.title: Validate Before You Ship
slides.subtitle: Quantization and sparsity need empirical verification.
slides.body: Run these 5 checks before productionizing V4.1 Flash.
slides.deep_dive: 1) Quantization fidelity: compare 4-bit vs 16-bit outputs on your task prompts. 2) Router stability: check expert utilization entropy—collapse means routing failure. 3) KV cache pressure: stress test context length at your max sequence. 4) Latency tail: measure p99 under concurrent requests. 5) Quality regression: run your golden eval set weekly. Treat the model as a new dependency: pin version, monitor drift.
slides.key_fact: Sparsity and quantization require task-specific validation.
slides.why_it_matters: Prevents silent quality degradation in production.
items: Stress test max context KV cache

slides.title: Local Frontier Models Arrive
slides.subtitle: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash makes 100B-class local inference real.
slides.body: Architectural sparsity + quantization breaks the VRAM wall. Verify on your tasks.
slides.deep_dive: The big picture: model efficiency is catching up to model capability. V4.1 Flash signals a trend—Mixture-of-Experts designed for consumer GPUs. Expect more releases targeting 12-16GB VRAM. For engineers: start building local-first architectures now. The API availability and licensing terms for V4.1 Flash are not specified in the source; check DeepSeek's official channels. The era of "too big for my GPU" is ending.
slides.key_fact: Designed-in sparsity enables consumer-GPU frontier models.
slides.why_it_matters: Shifts AI compute from cloud capex to local opex.
takeaways: Architectural sparsity > post-hoc quantization for VRAM
Run custom evals; no public benchmarks released
Design systems for local-first, cloud-optional deployment
